about: The polyglot task set (scripts/eval/tasks_polyglot.py): 30 Python exercises of aider's polyglot benchmark, chosen without looking at any solution (.meta/example.py and .approaches/ were never read; only .meta/config.json, the test files' test counts, the instructions' length and Exercism's difficulty rating).

source.license: no LICENSE file in the repository (GitHub reports none); its README says all exercises are copyright Exercism and used under Exercism's open-source licenses; the Python track (github.com/exercism/python) is MIT (checked 2026-10-30, its main at 6105f6d, 2026-09-30). Nothing of the exercises is copied into this repository: they are fetched at run time.
source.how_aider_chose_them: aider's blog (2024-12-21): of 697 Exercism exercises in six languages, the 225 solved by 3 or fewer of 7 then-current models; 34 of them are Python

rule: All 34 Python exercises, minus the 4 lowest by (Exercism difficulty, number of tests). Python only: Go and Node.js are not installed on the machine that runs the eval, so a JS or Go slice could not be pre-run (left for later).
gradient_note: aider publishes pass rates per model, not per exercise, so no exercise's pass rate for today's cheap models is known. The target (cheap model about half, strong models most) is a hypothesis: the direct arm of the first run (Codex gpt-6-luna low, no lead) measures the cheap model's rate. If direct gets 27/30 or more, this slice is at the ceiling too and is reported as such. Unlike aider (two tries, the second with the test errors), the tests stay hidden: closer to aider's first-try rate.
